enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
611 AM MDT Wed Oct 14 2026

...New AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 539 AM MDT Wed Oct 14 2026

 - Dry and seasonal temperatures through Thursday, with breezy
   afternoon winds.

 - A strong backdoor cold front is set to arrive Thursday night,
   bringing gusty winds and winter-like temperatures into the
   weekend. High Wind Watch is in effect for far west Texas and 
   portions of southern New Mexico. Wind gusts up to 60 mph are 
   possible along mountain west slopes. 

 - Freezing temperatures over area mountains may lead to a light
   wintry mix Saturday morning.

 - Mostly cloudy skies behind the cold front, with scattered rain
   showers Friday and Saturday, favoring west Texas.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1019 PM MDT Tue Oct 13 2026

Dry and breezy conditions are forecast for the short-term as an 
upper low scoots across the Four Corners. A trailing front will keep 
moisture and storm chances just east of our area for Wed. Drier air 
underneath the low will keep skies mainly clear with WSW winds of 10-
20 mph, gusting to 30 mph Wed afternoon. Winds shift N and E during 
the day on Thu as high pressure spills into the northern High 
Plains, slightly lower speeds than Wed. Temps remain near or just 
below normal under mostly sunny skies. 

A potent cold front arrives Thu evening from the NE, bringing strong 
E winds to the region Thu night into Fri. The strength of the sfc 
high behind the front is more in-line with what we tend to see in 
the middle of winter (1045mb-ish). This will result in an impressive 
pressure gradient across the CWA as the front sweeps through. West 
mtn slopes will see the gustiest winds, reaching 60 mph or higher
for peak gusts. Generally 25-35 mph sustained winds are modeled 
with a pocket of lighter winds from Las Cruces up to Holloman AFB.
No changes are being made to the High Wind Watch that's in effect
Thu night-Friday afternoon. The watch will be upgraded to at 
least an advisory at some point Wed with more advisories possible 
elsewhere. The strongest winds are expected to occur overnight Thu
into Fri morning with breezy winds lasting through Fri night. 
Recent rainfall should limit blowing dust concerns coming out of E
NM and W TX, but can't be ruled out due to the high winds.

A lobe of energy is modeled to break off from the upper low on Thu, 
pulling moisture from the south into the area late this week. Low-
medium rain chances move in Thu night for far west TX, lasting 
through Fri. Isolated to scattered rain showers drift NW into Sat. 
Hudspeth County is forecast to see the most rain with high 
uncertainty in rainfall amounts (0.25-0.5" for NBM 50th %-ile 
through Fri, 1.5-2.5" for 90th %-ile). Isolated flash flooding can
be seen, most likely in southern Hudspeth. Rain chances diminish 
as you head N and W. The much cooler temps may result in an early-
season rain/snow mix for the high terrain Sat AM if the moisture 
is advected far enough north around the upper low. Little to no 
snow accumulation expected due to the warm ground temps. 

The cut-off low off Baja should be picked up by a passing upper 
trough well to the north on Sun, shoving most of the moisture 
eastward, but leaving some over the Big Bend region. This remnant 
moisture looks to be scooped up by the next Pacific low into 
midweek, bringing more rain/storm chances to end the period. Low
confidence in impacts for this midweek system.

Temperatures will crash to unseasonably cool levels (highs 15-25 
degrees below normal) behind Thu night's front. Highs struggle to 
reach 60F for the lowlands Fri and Sat with strong cold air 
advection ongoing. It'll feel more like winter than early fall with 
some spots expected to see their first freeze of the season Sat or 
Sun AM as winds calm down. Temperatures rebound towards normal early 
next week as SW flow develops.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 611 AM MDT Wed Oct 14 2026

VFR conditions expected for the next 24 hours. Currently our
ceilings are unlimited across much of the area and those clear
skies will continue into the afternoon hours through Thursday
morning. Like yesterday, we will see another round of low end
gusty winds for a few hours this afternoon. The gusty winds will
drop off around sunset. 

Thursday evening a strong cold front will move across the area and
that will swing our winds around to the east and give us a lengthy
period of strong and gusty winds. The main impacted TAF sites for
the winds will be KELP, KLRU and KDMN. For Thursday night into
Friday, we will have winds of at least 08020G30KT with gusts to 50
knots possible.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 611 AM MDT Wed Oct 14 2026

Fire weather concerns will be limited today and most of Thursday.
Min RH's today will be above 20% and min RH's on Thursday will
range from the mid to upper teens in the lowlands to near 30% in
area mountains. We will have low end gusty winds this afternoon. 

On Thrusday evening, a strong back door (east to west) cold front
will move across the region. This front will swing our winds
around to the east and be strong. The strongest winds will be near
and west of area mountains where we could see wind gusts to 60
mph. Those strong winds will continue through Friday. On Saturday
we will see less winds, but it will still be breezy. Min RH's for
Friday through the weekend will be above 30% across the area. In 
addition to the strong winds, we will see a slight chance for 
lowland rain or high mountain rain/snow mix for Friday and 
Saturday. Precipitation totals look light both days.
